Neurologic, skeletal and ear abnormalities characterize the syndrome. Renal hypoplasia in 6/6 supports renal involvement. The four-axis cap reasonably prioritizes these over lesser anomalies.

Neurologic malformation defines Joubert syndrome. Polydactyly in 11/11, ocular malformations in 2/3 and renal hypoplasia in 1/3 support the three involved axes; small denominators justify medium confidence.
Metabolic encephalopathy defines the disease. Blistering skin injury in 30-79% and pancytopenia in 3/6 support involvement. Myopathy is appropriately acknowledged as omitted under the four-axis cap.

Defining lymphatic vessel and valve dysfunction supports the vascular mapping. Limb edema alone does not establish additional dermatologic damage or require inheriting the parent's dermatologic label.

Keratoderma, hearing loss and mutilating digit loss support the primary axes. Cognitive impairment at 30-79% supports neurologic involvement; qualifying endocrine involvement is acknowledged as omitted under the cap.
